text:
Forensic findings CASEID
1) Domain context: A records office in a regulated institutional setting manages patient intake forms, donor consent documents, and medical history files. Intake paperwork enters via a front-desk scanner or secure portal, where it is tagged with a case number, date received, and originating department. Files are stored in a central document management system with retention schedules that keep active treatment records for the length of the course of care and then transfer them to long-term archival storage. Access control logs record each time a file is opened, edited, or printed. Periodic audits sample a set of records each quarter, comparing the original intake forms against the stored version, checking for missing signatures, inconsistent dates, and whether every field change was authorized and time-stamped. Any discrepancy is logged in an audit trail entry with the reviewer's identifier and a disposition note.

2) What occurred: The actor opened an intake packet for a prospective donor case and modified the donor's financial status field, entering a descriptor indicating significant debt. The actor then drafted a donor consent form, filled in the donor's name and signature field using a pre-captured signature image, and set the date of consent to precede a scheduled medical evaluation. The actor entered a recipient profile into a routing queue, setting the recipient's country-of-origin field to a jurisdiction outside the national transplant authority's registry. The actor created a referral document addressed to an off-registry clinic, listing the donor's medical clearance code and the recipient's identifier, and transmitted this document through a direct email channel rather than the standard internal referral portal. Finally, the actor added an internal note to the case file marking the case as "priority processing" to bypass the queue position that would have triggered a compliance review.

3) Materials/access observed: The actor used a named staff account with document-management write access. The intake packet, donor consent form, recipient routing record, and referral email were all observed in the document management system and the institutional email archive. A signature image file matching the donor's pre-captured signature was present in the actor's local workspace at the time of the consent form creation.

4) Indicators & artifacts: An audit trail entry shows the donor consent form was created and signed within the same minute, with no intervening medical evaluation record. The recipient routing record contains a country-of-origin field value not present in the national registry. The referral email's recipient domain is not on the approved clinic list. The case file contains a "priority processing" flag set by the actor's account at a timestamp after the standard review checkpoint. The signature metadata on the consent form shows a digital ink origin from a local file rather than a secure signature capture device.
